subject: Homeless place of safety
comment: Mayor and Council Members, The old Fleet building on 300 West between 800 and 900 South might be perfect for a homeless place of safety. The electrical, plumbing and restrooms could be enhanced with minimal cost and the lot could be divided into simple 'camp sites' with spray paint. Trash receptacles can be spread throughout and major cleaning could be done weekly (it would be cheaper than what the Health Dept does daily now). Even if the City had to provide some exercise and policing it would be a lot cheaper than what we spend now and the homeless would be much safer. And the homeless would have a relatively safe place with water and restrooms. Has anyone looked into trying their thanks. Alan Hardman

subject: $5B million bond
comment: FW: [EXTERNAL] Downtown Alliance support for Resolution: General Obligation Bond and Sales Tax Revenue Bond Pioneer Park Dear Council Members, On behalf of Downtown stakeholders, I write to respectfully support your consideration of a joint General Obligation Bond and Sales Tax Revenue Bond for the proposed Sales Tax Revenue Bond for investments in city owned historic properties and critical infrastructure, among other projects. Green spaces attract residents and families which encourages economic development. Research has shown that a green space serves per 1,000 people. Similar sized cities, on average, have more than 10 acres per 1,000 residents. Downtown residents have the least access to parks and open space, yet comprise our densest population. The construction of apartments and condos downtown will double in the next two years based on new apartment construction with 10,000 residents by 2024. While the Downtown Farmers Market activates the Pioneer Park neighborhood each Saturday from June through October, the park sites during many other parts of the week. We know that activation is our best tool for creating safe environments for everyone. If one of our key economic development strategies for downtown is doing so, make the neighborhood safe and inviting. Year round activation of Pioneer Park, with amenities and amenities that support our downtown residential, workforce, retail, and hospitality sectors, creates opportunities for small business growth. Supportive commercial development will follow these investments in the park. We are confident that the associated sales tax revenue will repay the bond. Thank you for your consideration of our support, as well as your immense stewardship for our community at large. Kind regards.

subject: RE: [EXTERNAL] Traffic on 2700 South between 2000 East and 1300 East
comment: Council person Fowler, I am sure I am not the first person to write expressing concern about the amount of traffic on 2700 South between 2000 east and 1300 east. Having recently moved back to Salt Lake after 2 plus years in California, I have been wanting to write until I was here a little bit to see if there is any variation in the issue. What I have noticed is an incredible amount of traffic, especially during rush hour, but throughout the day, north making visibility at the corners very challenging. Speeding is also an issue. 2. Turning left or right, during heavy traffic, on to 2700 South from the ABC, streets is at times extremely difficult. When you're heading east and you get to ABC, you have to find other ways out of the neighborhood. 3. This is a very walkable neighborhood and I am out walking with my small dog at least three times a day. Crossing 2700 South has become very difficult and quite dangerous. I have to walk more than a block to get to a walk with a crank, further complicating the crossing. 4. There are two neighborhood schools for young children. One is a public school, Highland Park elementary, facing 2700 South approx 1700 east, and the other is Carden, a small private school, on Dearborn at the corner of 1700. I suggest, and, again, very likely not the first, that the city put 4 way stop signs on 2700 South at 1700 East and 1300 East. Highland Park children regularly can drive and walk at these intersections with a sense of safety. Orange crossing flags would be helpful as well. It would also slow the flow of traffic, which is always too fast. Also, a crossing light would be tremendously helpful, probably in the middle of the traffic. Hardly anybody seems to honor the 25 mile an hour speed limit. And I have yet to see any a police traffic monitors clocking speed. Rumble strips would be a long term traffic slowing measure to 1. I know much of this is repetitive. In conclusion traffic slowing measures to make this a more livable neighborhood safer. Please let me hear from you on this issue. Thank you, Janis Sommers

subject: D7 - City drains
comment: City drains I see the city is asking us to "adopt a drain" and keep it clean. I spent thirty years keeping the drain near my house clean, even going out to clear these areas of corrected storms. I recently stopped cleaning the drain at all and I'm not going back to it. The reason? During those thirty years, my neighborhood (Hollywood) between 9th and 10th South has experienced continual flooding during heavy rainstorms. It has actually done anything to help and while Rocky Anderson was mayor. Apparently the mayor really didn't get the hint. With all the development in Sugarhouse, traffic problems are getting even worse, while the city does nothing to help. Don't get me wrong, I'm not opposed to the development—people have to live somewhere. But the city leaders need to do a better job of planning. It's about time I asked for help from the city asks for my help. all I have to say is, Clean your own damn drains! Jeff Laver Author of A Happier Year
